title: Quarter-wave UV reflector with SWIR transmission window
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack designed for high reflection at 375 nm (center of 300-450 nm) will produce transmission peaks at harmonic wavelengths including the 1000-1700 nm SWIR band, enabling simultaneous UV rejection and SWIR transmission.
design_principle: Dielectric mirrors use constructive interference from alternating high/low index layers. Quarter-wave optical thickness at the target reflection wavelength creates maximum reflectance. Transmission windows occur at wavelengths where optical thickness equals half-integer multiples of the design wavelength.
proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2/SiO2)_12 | Fused Silica substrate, 24 layers total, starting with HfO2 on the air side
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers
deviation from quarter-wave thickness at 375 nm center wavelength
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 24 to stay under 30-layer limit
all thicknesses should be physically realizable (5-500 nm range)
HfO2 as first layer for mechanical durability on air side
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength and its odd harmonics
HfO2/SiO2 is a standard high-contrast dielectric pair for visible/NIR coatings
Transmission bands occur between reflection harmonics for periodic stacks
Starting with high-index layer on air side typically improves UV reflectance
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is manufacturable and well-understood
24 layers provides margin under 30-layer constraint for potential optimization
HfO2 offers good UV durability compared to alternatives like TiO2
known_risks: I recall HfO2 n≈2.0-2.1 and SiO2 n≈1.45-1.5 in visible/NIR but exact dispersion across 300-1700 nm is uncertain and must be read from registry data
Quarter-wave at 375 nm may not align perfectly with 1000-1700 nm transmission window - the 3rd harmonic would be ~125 nm and higher orders need verification
I am uncertain whether 12 pairs is optimal or if fewer pairs would suffice with better thickness tuning
Absorption in HfO2 below 400 nm is recalled but not quantified - could reduce UV reflectance efficiency
No angle specification in request - I assume normal incidence but this should be confirmed
execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric film on a fused silica substrate with air incidence, using only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Stack topology: Air | (hfo2/SiO2 (Lemarchand))_12 | Fused Silica, 24 layers total starting with hfo2. Optimize individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Total layer count must not exceed 30. Use normal incidence (0 degrees). Both polarizations should be considered equivalent at normal incidence. Layer thicknesses are the only design variables; material optical constants are read from registry measurements.
